masking.regex: identifiers were masked; person names are stored as written.
masking.regexNer: identifiers and person names were masked.

fromRun.maskedNone: No field was changed by masking.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every item of the exam with its result, scores and runs: failed first, then not run, passed and not yet scored.

ApiKeys.title: API keys
ApiKeys.description: Keys for programs that call the platform: the OpenAI-compatible API, agents and tools. Each key has the scopes you choose; the key itself is shown only once.
ApiKeys.emptyBody: Create a key for each program that calls the platform, with only the scopes it needs.
ApiKeys.name: Name
ApiKeys.revokeConfirm: Revoke the key "{name}"? Programs using it stop working at once.
ApiKeys.cidrsRequired: A key with impersonate needs allowed networks (one CIDR per line).
ApiKeys.scopesHint: Nothing is chosen for you: give the key only what its program needs.
ApiKeys.aclRoleHint: The role the key's knowledge searches run under; at most your own role.
ApiKeys.cidrsHint: Client networks in CIDR form, one per line; empty means any network.
ApiKeys.expiresHint: Optional. The key stops working at the end of this day (UTC).
ApiKeys.createdOnce: Copy the key now. It is not stored and will not be shown again.

Quotas.title: Quotas and limits
Quotas.description: Limits on requests, tokens and spend for the project, an API key or a user. Block refuses calls over the limit; warn lets them through and records a quota warning.
Quotas.emptyBody: Without a quota the project has no limit of its own.
Quotas.needsAdmin: Only a project admin changes quotas.
Quotas.label: Label
Quotas.scopeIdRequired: Choose the key or enter the user.
Quotas.numberInvalid: A whole number of 1 or more.
Quotas.scopeFixed: The scope cannot change after the quota is created.
Quotas.scopeUserHint: The id of a project member.
Quotas.actionHint: Block refuses the call (429); warn lets it through and records a quota warning.
Quotas.limitsHint: Leave a field empty for no limit.

Alerts.title: Alerts
Alerts.description: Alerts the platform raised, the rules that raise them and where they are delivered. Acknowledge an alert once it is handled.
Alerts.needsAdmin: Only an admin changes rules and notification settings.
Alerts.scopeHint: The installation's own alerts (services, disk and memory) are separate from a project's.
Alerts.emptyBody: Alerts appear here when a rule fires. Add rules on the Rules tab.
Alerts.capped: Only the newest {cap} alerts are listed.
Alerts.badge: {count, plural, =0 {No open alerts} one {# open alert} other {# open alerts}}
Alerts.badgeUnreadable: Open alerts could not be read
Alerts.rulesEmptyBody: Without a rule no alert is raised. Add one for each kind you want to hear about.
Alerts.recipientsRequired: An e-mail rule needs at least one recipient.
Alerts.thresholdsInvalid: Thresholds are whole percentages from 1 to 1000.
Alerts.kindsUnreadable: The alert kinds could not be read.
Alerts.kindHint: Only kinds the platform raises are listed.
Alerts.recipientsHint: E-mail addresses, separated by commas or spaces.
Alerts.thresholdsHint: Percent of the monthly budget; empty means 50, 80 and 100.
Alerts.webhookUrlHint: Empty: the default webhook of the notification settings.

notifications.title: Notification settings
notifications.description: Where e-mail and webhook alerts are sent from and to.
notifications.portInvalid: The port is a whole number.
notifications.passwordHint: Shown masked; leave it to keep the stored password.
notifications.webhookHint: Used by webhook rules without their own URL.
notifications.testRecipientHint: E-mail address or webhook URL; empty uses the settings.

Retention.title: Data retention
Retention.description: How long each kind of data is kept, for the installation and per project. A dry run shows what a pass would delete; the real run deletes it.

confirm.title: Delete data now?
confirm.body: This pass deletes every row past its retention period, for all data classes and projects. It cannot be undone.
confirm.dryRunHint: RETENTION_DRY_RUN does not apply to this button: it deletes even when scheduled passes are dry runs. Run a dry run first to see the counts.

Overview.title: Overview
Overview.description: The selected project at a glance: usage, approvals waiting for a person, open alerts and the newest runs.
Overview.unpriced: {count, plural, one {# request has} other {# requests have}} no price; {count, plural, one {its} other {their}} cost is not counted.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description: Tokens, cost and model requests of the selected project per day and per model (UTC days, from the platform's own usage records).
Usage.rangeInvalid: The range ends before it starts.
Usage.unpriced: {count, plural, one {# request has} other {# requests have}} no price; {count, plural, one {its} other {their}} cost is not counted.
Usage.noUsageBody: Usage appears once the project's models are called.
Usage.chartLabel: Input and output tokens per day

reasons.external_ref: Refers to another document ($ref outside this one).
reasons.ref_not_found: Refers to a part of the document that does not exist.
reasons.openapi_path_invalid: Its path is not safe to call (empty, . or .. segment, ?, #, \ or percent-encoded . / \).
reasons.operation_id_duplicate: Another operation has the same operationId.
reasons.operation_name_invalid: Its operationId cannot be a tool name (letters, digits, _ . -, at most 64).
reasons.parameter_location_unsupported: It uses a parameter location other than path, query or body.
reasons.parameter_name_conflict: Two of its parameters have the same name.
reasons.request_body_unsupported: Its request body is not a JSON object.

McpServers.title: MCP servers
McpServers.description: Publish an OpenAPI document or a remote MCP server as an MCP server of this installation. Choose the operations to serve and how the model sees them, then add the server to the tools.
McpServers.detailDescription: The operations this server serves, the upstream it calls and its last 24 hours.
McpServers.needsAdmin: Only a project admin can publish or change MCP servers.
McpServers.emptyBody: Publish an OpenAPI document, for example a BI tool's API, so agents can call its operations through MCP.
McpServers.name: Name
McpServers.keyHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Unique in the installation; the server answers under /mcp/ with this key.
McpServers.keyInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter (2 to 64 characters).

sourceKindHints.openapi: Each operation of the document becomes a tool; calls go to the upstream address.
sourceKindHints.remote_mcp: The tools of another MCP server, served here with this installation's guardrail, quota and log.

McpServers.upstreamHint: Scheme, host, port and path only. The installation's outbound policy applies; platform services are refused.

authHints.none: The upstream is called without credentials.
authHints.header: Sent as one header of your choice; transport and identity headers are refused.

McpServers.secretKept: The stored credentials are kept. Choose the type again or type new values to replace them.

accessHints.internal: Only this installation's agent runtime calls the server.
accessHints.token: API keys with the tools_invoke scope may call it too.

McpServers.guardrailModeHint: Makes the policy stricter, never looser: each rule runs in the stricter of this mode and its own.
McpServers.policyKeyHint: The key of the project's guardrail policy.
McpServers.specHint: OpenAPI 3, YAML or JSON, at most 1 000 000 characters. Paste it or read it from a file.
McpServers.deleteConfirm: Delete the MCP server “{name}”? Its address stops answering; a tool added from it fails until it is removed.

testResult.tools: {count, plural, one {# tool listed} other {# tools listed}}

McpServers.toolAdded: Added to the tools as {name}. Discover its actions there; they start switched off and needing approval.
McpServers.discovered: {count, plural, one {# operation found} other {# operations found}}
McpServers.opsHint: Only selected operations are served at the MCP address. The model sees the tool name and description; leave them empty to keep the operation's own.

noOpsBody.openapi: The document has no operations. Replace it with one that has.
noOpsBody.remote_mcp: Run “Discover tools” to read the tools the remote server lists.

monitoring.statusNote: OK: the upstream answered. Error: the request was made and failed, for example upstream_http_404, or the argument check refused it (invalid_arguments). Denied: refused before any request left, by a quota, egress, origin or path rule, for example quota_exceeded, egress_not_allowlisted or openapi_path_invalid (an unsafe path in the stored document or a caller's path value such as a/b). Blocked: stopped by the guardrail policy. The code says why. “Not OK” counts error, denied and blocked.
monitoring.emptyBody: Nobody called this server in the last {hours} hours.
monitoring.auditNote: Changes to this server are in the audit log as {actions}.

RunCards.approvalRole: Can be approved by: {role} or above
RunCards.approvalNote: Note (shown to the model on reject)
RunCards.approvalNoId: The approval cannot be decided here because the event did not name it.
RunCards.approvalWaiting: Waiting for approval by {role} or above. The answer continues here once it is decided.

Chat.title: Chat
Chat.noProjectBody: Pick a project in the top bar to see the assistants you can chat with.
Chat.noAgents: This project has no published assistant yet.
Chat.unavailableBody: "{key}" is not a published assistant of this project, or you cannot reach it.
Chat.deleteBody: It disappears from your list. Its messages are removed later under the retention policy.
Chat.runFailed: No answer: the run ended with {code}.
Chat.lost: The connection could not be resumed. The answer may still arrive; reload the conversation later.
Chat.pollFailed: Could not read the run: {message} ({code}). Trying again.
